story: At 9:17 on a sunny Tuesday night in Sumter Oaks, Gary is bench-testing the sound system and light wiring in his workshop, labeling each piece for the review. Over at Rosa's house, Donna offers to bring hay bales and sweet tea whenever Rosa's shifts leave an evening open, with Thursday suggested ahead of the parade. Hal is logging the written notices for Gary's golf cart and Donna's flamingos so they're ready for the 9 AM committee meeting, while Rosa sketches clip-on lights, a fabric banner, and a hay-bale skirt at her dining table.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Bench-test the sound system and light wiring at low volume, then label everything for the review
Hal (architectural review desk): Submit and log the written notices on Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos for tomorrow's 9 AM committee meeting
Rosa (rosa dining table): Pencil the clip-on lights, fabric banner, and tuck-on hay-bale skirt into the sketch for Hal

gary.thought_process: It's 9:17 PM and I'm home with nobody around. The Review application is still pending, and per L-01 I can't mount anything visible from the street until it's approved. I can still do honest prep, though: the wiring is hidden under the dash, and I can test the sound system on the bench at low volume well before 10 PM quiet hours. That way everything's ready the minute the committee signs off, and Rosa and I can walk the sketches over without any loose ends. Keeping busy with my hands beats sitting in a quiet house.

parameters.content: Bench-test the sound system and light wiring at low volume, then label everything for the review

donna.thought_process: Rosa is checking her shift schedule to find free evenings for building the cart. It's 9:17 PM on a Tuesday, and I already told her I'd pencil in the design and get it to Hal tomorrow. I shouldn't repeat myself. The useful next step is to help her pick a build night, so I'll offer a concrete evening and mention bringing supplies like hay bales. Keeping it short and moving things forward.

parameters.content: Whichever evening your shifts leave open, Rosa, just say the word and I'll bring the hay bales and a pitcher of sweet tea. Thursday would give us plenty of time before the parade.

hal.thought_process: I'm at Town Hall with nobody around. My notes say I wrote the notices on Gary's cart (L-01) and Donna's flamingos (L-02) last tick, so the paperwork exists. Standing around doesn't help. The architectural review desk is the right place to make sure the notices are properly filed, and the proposal drop box is for laws, which isn't my business tonight. By-the-book means the notices get date-stamped and logged before the 9 AM meeting. After that I can go home and rest.

parameters.content: Submit and log the written notices on Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos for tomorrow's 9 AM committee meeting

rosa.thought_process: Donna just agreed to the pumpkin patch plan with clip-on lights, the fabric banner, and a tuck-on hay-bale skirt, and she asked me to pencil it in so we can get it to Hal tomorrow. It's after 9 PM and I'm tired, but the dinner went well and the sketch is the whole point. Writing it down on the table sketch is the next concrete step, and I shouldn't repeat questions or invitations I've already made. Penciling in the hay-bale skirt keeps everything removable and Review-friendly under L-01, so Hal has something clean to look at tomorrow.

parameters.content: Pencil the clip-on lights, fabric banner, and tuck-on hay-bale skirt into the sketch for Hal

matters.text: Hal Weems: Submit and log the written notices on Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos for tomorrow's 9 AM committee meeting

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
